To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
bone collagen undergoes a number of posttranslational alterations with maturation and the cathepsin activity is increased toward more mature collagen.

the efficiency of cat hepsin K to degrade bone collagen is increased with the maturation of bone collagen, as shown by the increase in the collagen enzymatic cross-linking and in the isomerization of CTX isomers.
cathepsin-K preferentially solubilizes bone collagen that is more matured, as reflected by the increase in the extent of bone cross-links and CTX isomerized collagen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of bone collagen maturation on cathepsin-K-mediated collagenolysis.
the effect of bone collagen maturation on the susceptibility of bone collagen to cathepsin K.
the effect of collagen age on cathepsin-mediated bone collagen degradation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cathepsin K preferentially degrades the mature bone matrix.
cathepsin-K-mediated collagenolysis is a process which is not only dependent on the bone collagen content but also on the extent of bone matrix maturation.
cathepsin-K-mediated bone resorption may be more effective in matured bone collagen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cathepsin K preferentially solubilizes mature bone collagen.
cathepsin-K preferentially solubilize matured bone matrix.
cathepsin-K-mediated collagenolytic activity is higher in matured than in immature bone collagen, and that this effect is related to an increased affinity of catheptin K for β-isomerized CTX.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the efficiency of cat hepsin K to degrade bone collagen may be modulated by the extent of bone matrix posttranslational modification.
the collagenolyic efficiency of cathepstin K increases with the extent of bone maturation.
the collagenolytically active form of cathepsins K is the one that preferentially degrades the more matured collagen.
